### Building a New PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough that covers everything from selecting parts to powering up your first system. Feel free to skip sections you already know or dive deeper into any topic. --- ## 1. Plan & Budget | Item | Typical Cost | Notes | |------|--------------|-------| | CPU | $200–$500 | Core i5/i7/i9, Ryzen 5/7/9 | | Motherboard | $100–$300 | Match socket & chipset | | RAM | $50–$150 | 16 GB DDR4/DDR5 (2×8 GB) | | GPU | $200–$1500+ | Depends on gaming/creative needs | | Storage | $50–$200 | SSD (NVMe) + optional HDD | | Power Supply | $70–$150 | 550–750 W, 80+ Gold | | Case | $50–$200 | Mid‑tower, airflow | | Cooling | $30–$120 | Air cooler or AIO liquid | | Peripherals | $200–$400 | Monitor, keyboard, mouse | **Tip:** Use online PC builders (e.g., PCPartPicker) to check compatibility and price‑track parts. --- ## 2. Gather Your Tools | Tool | Why It’s Needed | |------|-----------------| | Phillips‑head screwdriver | Most screws | | Anti‑static wrist strap | Prevents static damage | | Thermal paste (if not pre‑applied) | Improves CPU‑cooler heat transfer | | Cable ties / Velcro straps | Keeps cables tidy | | Flashlight or headlamp | Good lighting in case of dim rooms | | Small container | Holds screws & small parts | --- ## 3. Prepare the Workspace 1. **Clean surface** – Flat, non‑conductive table or desk. 2. **Static precautions** – Ground yourself with an anti‑static strap or touch a grounded metal object before handling components. 3. **Organize parts** – Keep each component in its original packaging or a labeled bag. --- ## 4. Install the Power Supply (PSU) 1. **Place PSU** in the bottom rear of the case (most cases). 2. **Secure** with screws. 3. **Route cables**: - 24‑pin ATX to motherboard. - 8‑pin EPS (or 4‑pin) to CPU. - PCIe cables to GPU (if needed). - SATA power to storage. - 4‑pin Molex for legacy devices (optional). *Tip:* Keep cables as short as possible but avoid tight bends. --- ## 5. Mount the Motherboard 1. **Align standoffs** – Place the motherboard on the case tray, aligning screw holes with pre‑installed standoffs. 2. **Secure** with screws (do not overtighten). 3. **Check clearance** – Ensure no cables or components block the I/O ports. --- ## 6. Install the CPU 1. **Open the socket latch** (usually a lever). 2. **Align the CPU** – Match the triangle marker on the CPU with the one on the socket. 3. **Insert gently** – Do not force; the CPU should slide in. 4. **Lock the latch** back down. --- ## 7. Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler | Option | Steps | |--------|-------| | **Air cooler** | 1. Spread a pea‑size amount of thermal paste on the CPU.
2. Place cooler onto CPU, align screws.
3. Tighten screws in a cross pattern. | | **AIO liquid cooler** | 1. Attach pump block to CPU (thermal paste optional if pre‑applied).
2. Mount radiator to case (top or rear).
3. Connect pump to PSU via 12‑V fan header.
4. Connect fans to case fan headers. | --- ## 8. Install RAM 1. **Open DIMM slots** – Push the levers outward. 2. **Align** the notch on the RAM stick with the slot. 3. **Press firmly** until levers click back. 4. **Repeat** for all sticks. --- ## 9. Install Storage | Type | Steps | |------|-------| | **NVMe SSD** | 1. Locate M.2 slot on motherboard.
2. Insert SSD at ~45° angle.
3. Secure with screw. | | **SATA SSD/HDD** | 1. Slide drive into drive bay.
2. Secure with screws.
3. Connect SATA data cable to motherboard.
4. Connect SATA power cable from PSU. | --- ## 10. Install Graphics Card (GPU) 1. **Remove expansion slot covers** on the case where the GPU will sit. 2. **Insert GPU** into the top PCIe x16 slot. 3. **Secure** with screws. 4. **Connect power** – Usually 8‑pin or 6‑pin PCIe connectors from PSU. 5. **Check for proper seating** – Ensure the card is fully inserted. --- ## 11. Connect Front Panel & USB 1. **Locate front panel header** on motherboard (refer to manual). 2. **Match pins** – Connect power button, reset button, power LED, HDD LED, USB ports, audio jacks. 3. **Double‑check orientation** – Many connectors are keyed. --- ## 12. Cable Management 1. **Tidy cables** using ties or Velcro straps. 2. **Route cables** behind the motherboard tray for better airflow. 3. **Leave space** for future upgrades or additional drives. --- ## 13. Final Checks - **Verify all connections** – PSU, motherboard, GPU, storage, RAM, cooler. - **Ensure no loose screws** or stray wires. - **Close the case** – Snap or screw panels back on. --- ## 14. First Boot & BIOS Setup 1. **Power on** – Press the case power button. 2. **Enter BIOS** – Usually by pressing `Del` or `F2` during POST. 3. **Check hardware detection** – CPU, RAM, storage, GPU. 4. **Set boot priority** – SSD first, then USB/DVD. 5. **Save & exit**. --- ## 15. Install Operating System 1. **Create bootable media** – USB flash drive with Windows 10/11 or Linux distro. 2. **Boot from USB** – Select it in BIOS boot menu. 3. **Follow installation wizard** – Format SSD, install OS. 4. **Install drivers** – Motherboard chipset, GPU, Wi‑Fi, etc. 5. **Update Windows** or Linux packages. --- ## 16. Test & Benchmark - **Stress test** CPU/GPU (Prime95, 3DMark). - **Monitor temperatures** (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). - **Run games or workloads** to confirm stability. --- ## 17. Maintenance Tips - **Keep dust out** – Clean fans and filters every 3–6 months. - **Update firmware** – BIOS, GPU, SSD. - **Check thermal paste** after 2–3 years if temperatures rise. - **Backup data** regularly. --- ### Quick Reference Checklist | Step | Done? | |------|-------| | PSU installed | ☐ | | Motherboard secured | ☐ | | CPU seated | ☐ | | Cooler attached | ☐ | | RAM installed | ☐ | | Storage connected | ☐ | | GPU installed | ☐ | | Front panel wired | ☐ | | Cables managed | ☐ | | BIOS set | ☐ | | OS installed | ☐ | | Drivers updated | ☐ | | System tested | ☐ | --- #### Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | No POST / no display | Loose GPU or wrong power connector | Re‑seat GPU, double‑check power cables | | Overheating | Poor airflow or insufficient cooling | Add case fans, reapply thermal paste | | Random restarts | PSU under‑spec or faulty | Check PSU wattage, try another PSU | | BIOS not detecting SSD | SATA mode mismatch | Set SATA to AHCI in BIOS | --- ### Final Words Building a PC is a rewarding experience that gives you full control over performance and aesthetics. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help—happy building!
